title: Apricot Brief — ELI5 Policy Explainer
description: A warm-peach explainer layout pairing an illustrated question-poser with three numbered plain-language cards — closer to a Vox visual essay than a policy brief, with a single tangerine CTA anchoring the bottom.
philosophy: This template treats complexity as a design problem, not a content virtue. It exists to translate dense policy or regulatory language into three digestible, conversational beats without condescension or oversimplification. It refuses the cold grey neutrality of institutional newsletters and the anxious information-density of traditional civic explainers. It is built for writers whose audience opens email on a phone between tasks and deserves clarity without being talked down to.
goodFor: Civic-tech or govtech newsletters breaking down new regulations for general audiences
3-step 'how it works' explainers for public policy or consumer rights topics
Educational email campaigns simplifying tax, healthcare, or housing rule changes
Onboarding slides walking non-technical users through a multi-step process
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly data reviews requiring dense table layouts
Formal investor or board decks where illustrated characters undermine authority
Academic papers or legal documents that demand citation-rich, structured prose
Luxury or premium brand communications where warmth reads as low-cost
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the cover of a considered Vox explainer card — warm, unhurried, and inviting without tipping into juvenile. The illustrated character carries the editorial personality of the whole deck: curious, approachable, mid-thought. Compositional weight clusters in the upper-center, leaving the lower half open so the layout exhales rather than crowds. Avoid institutional flatness, anxious information-density, or any illustrated style that reads as generic clip-art — the character should feel deliberately drawn and editorially intentional.

examples.layoutNotes: Single-column centered layout with a generous outer margin (~10% each side) and no framing header band — the slide breathes open at all edges. The illustrated question-poser character anchors the upper-center zone, occupying roughly the top third of the vertical space. Title text stacks beneath the character — deck name large, topic or edition descriptor smaller — separated by a thin horizontal rule to carry hierarchy without weight contrast alone. A muted tangerine pill or label sits above the character as a category tag, grounding the identity before the eye reaches the headline.

examples.promptCore: Warm, sunlit editorial energy — closer to a friendly visual essay than a policy pamphlet, with three numbered cards offering a calm left-to-right narrative rhythm where each card is a self-contained conversational beat surrounded by enough air to prevent visual anxiety. An illustrated question-poser character grounds the upper portion with approachable humanity, signaling 'this was made for you' without a hint of condescension. The accent CTA pill at the base should feel like a gentle invitation rather than a demand — part of the warmth, not a hard interrupt. Avoid cold institutional flatness, anxious information-density, or any compositional stiffness that would make a reader feel like they opened a government form.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer breathing margin; three numbered explainer cards span the full content width below a short header zone, each card containing a large bold numeral, a one-line headline, and a two-sentence conversational body. An illustrated question-poser character is anchored to the upper-left quadrant — occupying roughly one-quarter of the vertical space above the card row — acting as a visual entry point that humanizes the topic before the cards take over. The tangerine CTA pill sits centered beneath the card row, padded generously above to let it breathe as a clear terminal beat. Hierarchy is driven by numeral scale contrast and subtle card-boundary rules; no heavy header band, no sidebar, and a minimal folio mark at bottom-right only.
